Needs changes before merge. SAFETY-tier review: two blockers.

The trial merge with upstream main `17b1b2b81c2fc555fdaa3f06dec73000d19d20c7` succeeded. All builds and tests ran locally. No GitHub runner was used.

The default refusal for legacy records is correct. The new flag survives the project and stream round trips. I checked all three changed NC goldens line by line. Only the initial Z words change: 14 to 16, 14.625 to 16.625, and 0.5512 to 0.6299. The revised fixtures explain these changes.

Requested before merge:

1. **[P1] Prove clearance between stock samples.** `crates/app/src/operation/g76_start.rs:149` checks isolated stations. It does not include the stock profile breakpoints or prove clearance between stations. A narrow stock rib can fall between samples. The function then sets `start_in_air = true` with material inside the rapid-infeed band.

   I reproduced this with the existing relief-groove unit test. Keep its wide-groove part and the 1.732 mm insert. Use stock with the same groove, but leave a radius-6 rib from Z13.16 to Z13.20. The rest of the groove floor stays at radius 4.5. The insert band is [13.134, 14.866]. Adjacent samples are approximately Z13.134 and Z13.2302, so neither sample meets the rib. With no prior cuts, the existing assertion fails:

   ```text
   panicked at crates/app/src/operation/g76_start.rs:289:9:
   uncut stock in relief groove must refuse
   ```

   Use a conservative interval check for remaining stock and prior-cut coverage. Include profile breakpoints. Refuse the cycle when clearance cannot be proved. Add a regression for material between samples. The radial sampling also needs a conservative clearance rule.

2. **[P2] Supply the required heavy-lane results.** The PR body's Tests section lists the quick gate and clippy only. Current upstream `AGENTS.md`, “Heavy lanes at review”, requires the reached lanes and their results in the body. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` reaches the motion and app heavy lanes. Run these lanes on the corrected final head and record their results. Heavy tests were not run in this review. Their status is not a pass.

Requested before merge:

1. **Move the clearance geometry to its domain crate.** `crates/app/src/operation/g76_clearance.rs:4` introduces a geometry module in `app`. `AheadCut`, `covers`, and `rectangle_clear` use only coordinate values, insert dimensions, and pilot dimensions. They do not access the ECS world, a project file, a command, MCP, or the CLI. Current upstream `AGENTS.md`, “app holds the document, nothing else”, requires this code in the owning domain crate. Move the coverage algorithm and its focused tests to `camcraft-motion` or the owning geometry crate. Pass the cut and pilot values through its API. Keep the operation collection and document integration in `app`. Retain the narrow-rib, radial-gap, and diagonal-blade regressions.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 3c3f8b1d8b72b225459a63d71948f15c2c100267 -->
Read-only second review (Opus). Not built here.

Verdict: Needs changes before merge.

The Fanuc part of the change is correct as far as I can read it. The one blocker is a tracking item: it needs no code change.

## Blockers

1. **The same rapid-infeed defect stays open in the Tormach post, and no issue tracks it.**
   - `assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps:826-852` writes the LinuxCNC one-block G76. The LinuxCNC cycle also moves to the depth of each pass at rapid traverse from the drive line at the start Z.
   - `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/thread_g76_mm.nc:12-13` still shows `G0 Z14` then `G76 P2 Z8 ...`. That fixture bar continues past Z14, so this is the #2878 defect in a second dialect.
   - `crates/app/tests/lathe_post_tormach_thread.rs:282-285` must now set `start_in_air = true` by hand to keep the Fanuc output of that fixture. This shows that the fixture start is not in free air.
   - The decision file and the PR body say "a follow-up", but I find no filed issue.
   - Required: file a `source:agent` issue (P1 by the priority table, `area:post`, `area:turning`, `effort:high`) for the Tormach G76 refusal on `StartInAir`, and name it in the PR body. A code change in this PR is not required.

## Notes (not blocking)

1. **Where the law is judged.** `g76_start::judge` (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:3315`) runs only in the unposed (`frame` is `None`) verify arm. It replaces the motion flag with a check against the revolved part, the setup stock and the prior turned cuts. The prior cuts come from `rest::turned_ahead` (the recorded moves of earlier Turn-family ops). Threading reads the prior digest in `stamp.rs`, and `digest_of` now hashes the blade half-width. Thus an edit of an earlier Facing or Grooving op makes the thread stale, and the post refuses it until it is regenerated. In a posed setup the motion flag stays. That flag requires the raw stock top in front of the band (`thread_cycle.rs:146-150`), which is conservative.
2. **Proof shape.** `g76_clearance::rectangle_clear` accepts a cell only when all four corners are in one convex removed set (capsule of one sign, blade sweep with outward ray, capped drill cone). The stock profile breakpoints bound each interval. The cell budget refuses when exhausted. I find no case where material between stations is credited. Unreadable stock and a failed frame give `false`.
3. **Axial clearance.** The part check (`part_band_clear`, `thread_cycle.rs:53-62`) uses only `HAIR`. An insert band edge can pass the end face or a groove wall at almost zero gap. The stock check uses the gouge margin. Think about the same margin (tightened by the model excess) for the part check in a follow-up.
4. **Flank infeed direction.** `cycle_infeed_band` shifts the deep pass toward the end of the thread (`dir`). Issue #1842 says that the Fanuc Z-shift reading is not verified. A band that covers `start_s +- shift` on both sides costs little, and stays safe if that reading is wrong. Recommended for #1842 or a follow-up.
5. **Out of scope by design.** The Threading kernel is OD only and cylindrical (one root), and `lead` is the pitch (one start). Thus internal, taper (R word) and multi-start threads do not occur here. An ID record would refuse, because the part silhouette stands above the root. The blade credit in `AheadCut::covers` is outward only. An ID groover, if one is added later, must not get this credit (the `Meridian::outward` comment states the same rule).
6. **Posted text.** The three changed goldens change only the start Z: `Z14.` to `Z16.`, `Z14.625` to `Z16.625`, `Z0.5512` to `Z0.6299`. The fixture bar now ends at Z14.693 (free face), and the 1.732 mm insert band at Z16 is Z15.134 to Z16.866, which is 0.44 mm clear of the face. The two G76 blocks, the Q words in microns without a decimal, R and F are unchanged. The refusal is the last check in `g76Why`. It runs before any block is written, and `g76_refuses_when_start_point_is_inside_a_solid_bar` asserts that no file is written.
7. **G32.** The G32 writer does not change. The G32 output of a fixture changes only where its `top_z` changed: `a_right_hand_thread_posts_toward_the_chuck_under_m03` now has eight half-turns from Z15 instead of six from Z13. This comes from the `k_hi` change in `thread.rs:245`. That change lets a pass start in front of the end face for G32 output too, when the Top of Part Z stands above the face.
8. **Overlap with PR #2889 (issue #2879).** This PR contains the #2879 change: the same `revolve.rs` hunk and a `thread.rs:245` hunk on the same line. #2889 uses `station_of(top_z)` without `.max(s_hi)`. The PR that merges second gets a conflict on that line. Keep the `.max(s_hi)` form, because it never makes the lattice shorter than the window. Add `Refs #2879` to this body. The `revolve.rs` change removes only out-of-domain window ends, because the in-domain band edges are already in the lattice.
9. **Project file.** `start_in_air` is derived data, not a user parameter, so it needs no command and no MCP tool. Old caches and streams read `false` and refuse G76 with "regenerate the operation". This is safe. The maintainer's comment on #2878 reads the defect as a general approach problem. This PR answers the G76 part only.
10. **Code shape.** `generate.rs` grows by 5 lines (one `mut`, one call). All new files are under 400 lines. The geometry is in `camcraft-motion`, and the document collection is in `app`. No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests. The float math is guarded by `is_finite` checks.
11. **Tests.** 12 `#[test]` added and none removed or ignored. Tests that changed assert the new start Z and `AIR 1`. They are not weaker. A relief-groove start that posts end to end through the Fanuc post is pinned only at unit level (`g76_start::tests`). An end-to-end post test would be useful.
12. **Earlier reviews.** The findings of the two earlier "Needs changes" reviews are met at this head: the rectangle proof with the breakpoints, the heavy-lane results, and the move of the geometry to `camcraft-motion`.

## Gates and merge

- By the body, on this head: the quick gate fell back to the batch tier (956 steps, 0 failed), clippy on the four crates was clean, and the motion and app heavy lanes ran (220 steps, 0 unexpected failures, with the three known #1950 expected failures). The release tier did not run.
- Trial merge with the current `origin/main` `88805e692`: clean (`git merge-tree` tree `aac21761c`). Since the base, main changed `generate.rs` in other arms (`relief_zones`, rotary picks), and added no literal of `ThreadCycle`, `ThreadRec`, `TurnedAhead` or `Ahead`.
- A gate on the merged tree must run, at minimum:
  - `camcraft-app` lib (`operation::g76_start::tests`, `turning_rapids_tests`), `lathe_post_g76_start`, `lathe_post_g76`, `lathe_post_g76_schedule`, `lathe_post_g76_sources`, `lathe_post_inch`, `lathe_post_tormach_thread`, `lathe_post_tormach_g76_ladder`, `lathe_post_thread_dips`, `lathe_post`, `conformance`, `solid_law_goldens`, `program_units`.
  - `camcraft-motion`: `turning_g76_clearance`, `turning_thread_cycle`, and the other `turning_thread*` binaries.
  - `camcraft-post`: lib, `inverted_post`, `recorded_streams`. `camcraft-cl` lib.
